narration: Welcome to the Harappan section of the museum. Here you’ll find a small terracotta figurine from Mohenjo‑daro, dating to about 2700‑2100 BCE. The figure shows a pregnant woman with an elongated, muzzle‑like animal face, standing only 9.4 by 4 cm tall. A round cavity on its head suggests it once held an attachment that has since been lost. While we don’t know its exact ritual role, it offers a fascinating glimpse into the symbolic world of the Indus Valley civilization.
